title: 35 College Students, 32 Cheated in Exams Professor Uses a Hidden Spell to Expose AI
excerpt: Professor Jason Gibson's recent TikTok video has received over ten million views, revealing a shocking and amusing situation: out of 35 students in his two clas
content_html:
Professor Jason Gibson's recent TikTok video has received over ten million views, revealing a shocking and amusing situation: out of 35 students in his two classes, 32 failed the midterm exam because they all used AI-generated answers without even checking them.

Gibson's anti-cheating method was clever and elegant. He embedded a hidden prompt in the exam with white text that is invisible to the naked eye. If students simply copied the questions into an AI tool, this hidden instruction would cause the AI to generate a meaningless sentence containing "Madagascar." When grading the papers, the sudden appearance of the word "Madagascar" in all 32 answer sheets exposed the cheating immediately.

After the exam, Gibson publicly explained the method of screening for cheating and provided an opportunity for appeals. In the end, only 2 out of the 35 students chose to appeal. Gibson shared in his video the absurd "Madagascar" sentences generated by AI, which sparked a heated discussion on social media about AI and academic integrity.

This incident has hit upon a common anxiety facing global education systems: as AI tools become easily accessible, the traditional exam format's ability to prevent cheating is rapidly becoming ineffective. Students no longer even need to read the AI output before submitting it - in Gibson's case, if anyone had glanced at those strange paragraphs about Madagascar, the entire class wouldn't have collectively failed. Perhaps the more urgent question is not "how to stop students from using AI," but rather: when the basic willingness to check AI answers is disappearing, how much of the educational foundation remains?

content_html_zh:
Jason Gibson教授最近发布的TikTok视频点击量破千万，揭露了一个令人震惊又搞笑的情况：他的两个班的35名学生中，有32人期中考试不及格，因为他们都使用了人工智能生成的答案，甚至连检查都没有。

吉布森的反作弊方法巧妙而优雅。 他在考试中嵌入了一条肉眼看不见的白色文字的隐藏提示。 如果学生只是将问题复制到人工智能工具中，这种隐藏指令将导致人工智能生成包含“马达加斯加”的无意义句子。 批卷时，32张答卷中突然出现“马达加斯加”一词，作弊行为立即暴露。

考试结束后，吉布森公开解释了筛查作弊的方法，并提供了申诉的机会。 最终，35名学生中，只有2人选择上诉。 吉布森在视频中分享了人工智能生成的荒唐“马达加斯加”句子，引发了社交媒体上关于人工智能和学术诚信的热议。

这一事件触及了全球教育系统面临的普遍焦虑：随着人工智能工具变得越来越容易获取，传统考试形式的防作弊能力正在迅速失效。 学生们甚至不再需要在提交之前阅读人工智能输出——在吉布森的例子中，如果有人浏览过那些关于马达加斯加的奇怪段落，整个班级就不会集体失败。 也许更紧迫的问题不是“如何阻止学生使用人工智能”，而是：当检查人工智能答案的基本意愿消失时，教育基础还剩下多少？
